posts.cooked:
I still think Fixer is one of the weaker heroes (not that the gulf is large).  Sure, he can dish out a lot of damage with a good setup, and has somewhat better odds of a good setup than other heroes who can do better.  But he's still fairly limited in the range of effects he can produce.  No Ongoing destruction, no villain deck control, little ability to contribute if heroes can't use Powers, even less if they can't play cards in the early turns, and virtually none if he can't deal damage, unless he has one of a very small number of powerful utility cards in his hand (Grease Gun, Salvage Yard, am I forgetting anything?).  That combined with the fact that many of his card plays sabotage each other make him fairly narrow and situational.  He can be an all-star in certain situations that are not exactly rare, but he can't always be counted on to help, and he only rarely proves the best contributor.

Compare all this to, say, Tempest or The Argent Adept.  It's clear that, while the heap is pretty evenly-distributed, there are heroes which are at the top, and Fixer is at the bottom.  (Although given that I can name more very-strong heroes than very-weak ones, perhaps "heap" is the wrong metaphor..."trench" perhaps?)

The trick with Fixer, as I see it, is that he gets some unusual effects.  DR cancellation and damage type manipulation are fairly unusual.  If those are the tools you need, Fixer is your man.  But if that isn't what you need, or you can't get the right tools or stances, then he's weaker than average.

 

Which is just another way of saying that he's situational, which is what everyone else is saying.  But I guess what I'm saying is that when Fixer is MVP, it's because he's doing something that nobody else can do, which is why he makes up for it by being meh when his skills aren't critical.  And DW Fixer can help fill in when he needs a bit more oomph instead of surgical precision.

Agree with jzs2.  Bunker can make the same claim; no other character can embed the Paparazzi of Megalopolis in adhesive foam for three full turns.  But he is also mediocre much of the time, and has to do a lot of work getting there.  Such characters might be your "go to guy" if assembling a team for a particular foe, but they are often weak if selected randomly or at-whim.

awp832:

Darkwatch Fixer, however, is a game changer…  primarily because of Riveting Crane Style.    Strike is often too weak by itself to get in the 1 point of damage needed to take advantage of Riveting Crane.   However,  when Bitter Strike is added to the mix,  fixer can strip damage reduction off of a boss or even off of several minions at a time.

But only about half of villains use reduction, and it's often not their most salient form of invincibility.  Spite and Iron Legacy both rely more on healing, which no hero yet published (possibly excepting Vengeance, I don't know there) can prevent, although at least one Environment does reduce it a bit.  ATC and RC styles are completely useless against villains who don't rely on DR as a way to protect themselves (for instance I believe Plague Rat has just a single copy of a DR card, which might as well not exist given that he provides no secondary targets to distract the heroes from whaling on him).  Against someone like Warlord Voss or advanced Miss Information, Fixer is an all-star…but the second or so time I played him, we were up against La Capitan, and only one of her minions even has reduction (while another has healing, grrrr).  Fixer only has the tools (or Tools) to fix certain problems; others remain insoluble, and Fixer isn't always worth the +1 to H that his presence generates, or the slot he takes away from a different hero.

Driving Mantis is one of my favorite cards when paired with; Dual Crowbars, Assault Rifle, Thermal Shockwave, Taiaha and Puninsh the Weak, Inferno, Cerebral Hemorrhage, Danny-boy, Chain Lightning... I think people get where I am going with this.

Riveting Crane is one of my favorite cards when going last against Voss, when Mega Computer is in play, or when hitting a target with DR.

Alternating Tiger Claw is one of my favorite cards when there is a ton of DR!

Grease Monkey is one of my favorite card when any of the other 3 styles are not my favorite card.

Jack Handle is one of my favorite card when there are bunches of targets to hit or when Fixer would be forced to hit himself or another hero.

Dual Crowbars is one of my favorite cards when there are a couple of targets that I want to hit, when I have Driving Mantis to redirect my second hit, or when I am forced to hit myself or an ally so I can still hit the enemy.

Hoist Chain is one of my favorite cards when a solo target is dealing most of the damage, when I want to help protect an ally, or paired with Driving Mantis to help redirect damage.

Tire iron is one of my favorite cards when Fixer is on beating the lowest target duty or when the current tool can't quite do the damage needed to finish the job.

Pipe Wrench is one of my favorite card when I feel like being a jerk and carrying only about my own safety, when pairing with Driving Mantis to redirect damage, to remain the highest hero target when mostly the highest is being hit.

Salvage Yard is one of my favorite cards when my allies need equipment back ASAP.

Overdrive is one of my favorite cards because I can use the same power twice in a single turn or when I need a slight boost in damage.

Charge is one of my favorite cards when I need to beat things multiple times.

Bloody Knuckles is one of my favorite cards when it can do exactly the right amount of damage when I need it to.

Meditation is one of my favorite cards when I want to stand in a better position than currently am in.

Tool Box is one of my favorite cards so I can discard cards for allies and not care about it or move through my deck faster.

Grease Gun is one of my favorite cards when heroes need a break from non-hero targets.

Harmony is one of my favorite cards when I have achieved inner peace.

Every card in Fixer's deck is one of my favorite cards when it is in my hand.

Firstly, someone will most likely say "DR will hurt that, because DR always exist, bleh... bleh... bleh..." There are 7 heroes capable of increasing damage. There are also 5 environments that also increase all damage, also the Tomb of Anubis that can give a power that deals a base of 2 damage, making it 6 Environments that can help increase Fixers damage output.

Lets start with the "I can't draw what I want/need!!!"

Now it is true each one of his cards are best in different situations, but that doesn't mean other cards cannot work in the situation they are not best for.

Looking at the tools first, how many of these are super restrictive in their uses? Tire Iron is the only one I can think of, as targets need to be quite low on health for it to work, but tools have the added benefit of returning to hand when playing another, so it may be worth slapping that down when it is needed to get a killing blow, then switching back to the other tool the following turn.

Jack Handle is certainly best when facing tons of targets or when forced to hit heroes. How many villains have very low target count and do not force heroes to hit themself? Spite, that's all. So the majority of the time, it's a pretty good card to keep in play. Sure it may not help every turn, but when the villain makes Fixer try and hit a hero for 2 damage, it's great that he does it to all non-heroes instead.

Dual Crowbars functions a lot like Jack Handle, in two targets are great! But it also has that +1, so even against someone like Spite, you still get a benefit. Even when forced to hit another hero, you get to hit the big bad as well. So once again, never a bad time to play it.

Hoist Chain, it reduces damage a target can deal... I can't see any reason why this would be a bad card to play... I certainly don't hate seeing it in my hand.

Finally Pipe Wrench, +1 damage dealt and -1 damage taken. Good, all around card. Never is painful to have it being the only tool available.

My thought process says Tools are actually quite diverse, with only Tire Iron being very restrictive on when to use it. Jack Handle being a distant second because of Spite. Everything else can be the one in play, even if it's not the best tool for the job.

I am not going to do the same thing with the Styles, as they are the most restrictive between Style and Tools. But that is why they have Meditation. But even so, Gease Monkey Fist or Driving Mantis are never bad to have in play.

Lastly we have Grease Gun, Harmony, Bloody Knuckles, Tool Box, Salvage Yard, Charge, and Overdrive. Salavage Yard is really the only card that is worth holding on to. Harmony should probably be first even without a Style or Tool in play, just so that way when you get both you'll get the bonuses right then. Unless of course you need damage immediately, Bloody Knuckles would typically be first for me, unless I know I am going to be hit a lot. Grease Gun of course saved for just whenever mostly.

I've had games where I had only one card in play, and I still kicked ass because of Bloody Knuckles, Charge, and Overdrive. After all, if I am not drawing Styles and Tools, then I am drawing the great One-Shots or Bloody Knuckles.

It's only 8 cards in the deck that will most likely have no use at all, if those are the first 8 cards someone draws, then that's some bad shuffling.

This is actually the case for most heroes... Wraith wants to focus on damage, Razor Ordinance, Throwing Knives/Stun Bolt, Utility Belt, and Micro Targeting Computer. What else does she have to do? It would also fit his theme of “right tool for the right job” a lot better if he didn’t have to spend a few turns switching his setup every time the situation changed. I like Mister Fixer as he is, but he is definitely a Johnny type character. You do interesting things with him that only work out every once in a while.

I don’t think his consistency problem is that he doesn’t have deck search for tools. I think its that he doesn’t have the ability to aim for late game effectiveness or early game effectiveness. Characters like Wraith can aim for long term setups that do a whole bunch of things at once, with 5 or 6 different pieces of equipment all providing valuable help, while still keeping pace before getting fully setup. Whereas Ra can be doing powerful things from turn 1, even if he doesn’t change that significantly when given time to set up. Fixer can only have 1 style, 1 tool, and harmony in his set up. And Harmony only matters if he has one of the other two. None of the styles and tools are so amazing that you can beat face with one of them on turn one. And you don’t have very much room to grow to achieve late game dominance. So it feels a lot like you are struggling for competency. Medium risk, low reward. His best stuff is finding small tricks like going last against Voss to negate DR. It feels satisfying for finding unconventional workarounds to problems your team faces. He at least has that to recommend him over Expatriette. He has a lot of good cards, and a lot of good ways to use them. But not enough synergy with himself.

I really like Mantis stance.  One thing that might hinder my play with Fixer is that I like it too much.  If I have it in play and don't have another copy I'm really hard pressed to change to a different stance.  I feel like even if the other stance is better this round it hinders me for each round thereafter.

 

On another topic.  Duplicate limited cards are not a problem for some heros because they have something to do with them.  Nightmist and Scholar are prime examples as any duplicate just makes choosing your discards easier.  Even Wraith has Trust fund with which to replace duplicate cards with different cards.  Fanatic and Tempest can always discard them for damage from ongoings, etc.  Heck if you have nothing to do with them but enough draw that they don't hinder getting to your juice that is fine too.  Other heros have nothing to do with them, Legacy for examle can't do anything with a second ring.  Fixer has what seem like an unusually large number of limited cards for someone that can't use or cycle them.  Duplicate tools get you no where, (except if your equipment is destroyed and it no longer a duplicate though that is always true).  Duplicate stances are not as bad as then you can swap and later swap back alleviating my issue above.  But again seeing several copies of a seldom used stance gets tiresome.

 

So I said previously that Fixer has amazing abiltiy but it often doesn't line up with play. Here is an example, please don't get too bogged down in the specifics of the example and more the point because I already know it was a tough situation for other heros as well.  I'll reiterate the exact point at the end.  I'll try to remember it accurately:

We are fighting dreamer and she puts out two Dark Hero's on the same turn.  This means that every projection is at 2DR.  My friend is playing Fixer and I'm optimistic.  He says "well I have a couple copies of the stance in my had that lets me get rid of DR."  I smile, then comes, "but I don't have a way to get through the DR to apply that."  I look at his board, He hasn't hit a Harmony all game leaving his damage at 2, not enough.  I say, "What about the stance that let YOU ignore DR, that and crowbars would be a good start?"  "Nope, haven't seen it, don't have meditation."  I say, "do you have a charge or bloody knuckles? you can set up this turn and bust through next turn" "Nope, in my had I have two tire irons, two (the DR removing stance), a jack handle, and an overdrive none of which helps.  Well, I'll just draw two cards and hope for something good."  Draws two cards, "Nope, I still suck."

 

The point is that Fixer definitely has the tools (pun intended) in his deck to deal with this situation, and in fact a couple different ways.  We knew them, we identified them, we were unable to execute them.  I know that this can happen to every hero, but at least for us it happens significantly more with Fixer.  I stated before that I like decks to be able to do what they are intended to do, but with him it feels like he has so much potential but that potential is often not realized.  I'm actually wondering if he does well a fair amount of the time, but he falls short often enough that it really stands out more because people know he has potential.  To have the solutions in your deck but not be able to get them is frustrating and off putting.

Ronway:

So Infrared Eyepiece becomes a good play in games where you are focusing on damage when the Villain becomes immune? Wow, that seems oddly situational. So you don't like how Fixer plays cards when their best situation comes up, but it's fine to already have a card in play if it may be useful later?

If I'm not doing anything else with my play phase, then sure, why not?  The only exception would be if I was worried about a wipe (in particular Technological Singularity); in those cases I'd keep the cards in my hand rather than store them on the table.  But if I'm against heavy discard which isn't Citizen Dawn (since she can both discard and wipe), then it's particularly handy to keep things in play just in case.  And, all other things being equal, I'd just rather play more cards.  I also like drawing more cards; I don't much care for having cards and not using them.

It's not a disadvantage to have to bounce cards back in hand. It's actually a balancing mechanic so that way Fixer won't be able to deal all targets 3 damage, twice, kill anything with 2 or fewer hit points, and anything surviving will reduce their damage by 2. Then imagine if Fixer also played Overdrive or Charge.

Right, I'm not really arguing with that part.  Like I said, if Fixer's Styles also went back to his hand, and if he had better card drawing or searching, I'd probably be okay with him.  But as is, he's just got too many deficiencies, and my terrible luck exagerrates them, so I find him very frustrating to play.  (A lot of people have had similar complaints about Bunker and AZ, but both of those "like" me; my Bunker games get a tad repetitive since I usually just Flak Cannon everything, but I've had The God-Turn with AZ at least a couple times, and find it totally worth how hard it is to set up, which is completely not how I feel about Fixer going Jack Handle + Monkey Fist + Harmony + Bloody Knuckles + Charge, even if that result might be objectively better than Hoarfire + both Modules and one or both of the other Equipment.)

Only if you're not keeping the Villain and Environment decks cleaned up. At most he'll typically only take 4 extra damage, it's perfectly survivable.

You do know that most villain and many environment targets deal damage at the end of the turn they come into play, right?  And that many ways exist for these decks to play an extra card?  I've seen three or four new damage instances pop out of nowhere on multiple occasions, and sometimes they hit all heroes, or the lowest hero.  I'm disinclined to take that kind of risk.

What's wrong with skipping a turn to prevent all non-hero targets from doing damage?

Ask Haka or Tachyon that question and hear them laugh.

Fixer is in every game that Salvage Yard is in, if heroes manage to go through most of a game without Equipment being destroyed, there should still be an Overdrive in the trash you can use it for instead.

Overdrive is just 1 extra damage unless you have a good "rig" set up, which as I have established, I often don't.  I seldom want to waste a card as theoretically-powerful as Salvage Yard on that little benefit, but often its potential is never actualized.  I think I've seen it perform extremely well twice, out of nineteen games.  It shows up in my hand in at least half of them, but usually the heroes aren't trashing enough Equipment for it to matter, and Fixer might never even draw Overdrive, though it's probable that he will.

Charge+Strike deals 3 damage, more than Haka's base power.

The comparison should not be Fixer's card and power to just Haka's power.  Throw in an Elbow Smash and Haka is now doing 5 damage.  And Elbow Smash in turn is pathetic next to Ra's Flame Blast plus his power.  Or if 3 damage is all we need, Legacy can do it with just a card play, perhaps drawing a card as a result, and then Galvanize everyone.

Besides, how often do you play either of those cards when you have nothing in play?

If they're all I have that's worth playing, but the team needs my pathetic 1 damage so I can't draw 2, then damn if I'm not going to play a pathetic card rather than no card, if I'm not going to get anything for giving up my play phase.  I make very few exceptions to the rule that I perform either both of my non-draw phases, or neither of them.

I don't play them unless…I really need to squeeze out a few points of damage to kill something.

Which is pretty much always in my experience.  (Except against Ambuscade or Miss Information.)

That would mean you are drawing the same 10 cards almost every game.

Explains a lot of my attitude doesn't it?  But as I've said, this doesn't seem to cause me any problems when I'm virtually any other hero (except maybe Bunker, as mentioned above, and there the problem is just homogeneity, rather than utter patheticness).  My repetitious games as Visionary, Nightmist, Unity, Tachyon, Haka, Tempest, Wraith, and other card-drawing heroes are self-correcting.  With AZ, I go several games without seeing cards like Fueled Freeze or Thermal Shockwave, but who cares?  Once I've got my two modules (with twelve total cards ensuring that at least one of them gets into play), I'm golden; I'll make do with whatever's in my hand.  No other hero suffers anywhere near the level of failure I've had as Fixer; Expatriette and Unity are the closest, since one needs a Gun and the other at least a Golem, but I've generally gotten the problem fixed within two turns at most.  Ironically, Fixer can't Fix himself without his Tool Box, which is why it probably ought to be a 4-of in his deck, or else a search card that gets you Tools the way Meditation gets Styles.  I've also had a few sluggish games with Argent, and this is one of the reasons I rank him fairly low in spite of his immense potential; Legacy is dead last in my rankings, and he also has some of the problems I face with Fixer, such as never drawing Flying Smash, and Danger Sense or Superhuman Durability usually being blank cards (however my bigger problem with Legacy is just that he's boring, since his Power phase consists almost exclusively of waving a pair of pom-poms instead of actually doing anything - he needs the Legacy Ring as badly as Fixer needs Tool box, and once again, he gets only two copies of it).

Against Voss, Fixer can hit Voss without any DR, then anyone hitting Voss while a Minion is in play will be able to do Irreducible damage.

Very seldom will a window open up for this to be feasible.  Voss starts the game with Minions in play, and flips when they're gone.  For this scenario to apply, he'd have to have no minions when Fixer strikes him, but then gain some during subsequent hero turns or the Environment turn.  Otherwise, he'll be flipped and have maybe 1 point of DR at the most, so Riveting Crane will be a very minor buff.

Against Advanced Omnitron, every other round Fixer can hit Omnitron's non-DR side and when he flips, the DR no longer matters.

Now that actually is a decent idea.  I'm not sure if I've played Fixer against Omnitron.  Not that Omnitron needs any help losing games, of course, unless he's Cosmic.  Still, maybe a 3-hero game would be worth trying.

Chairman, Deputy is in play, bringing out the Crooked Cop. The heroes can work together to kill the Crooked Cop with AoE while focusing on Operative, Fixer can hit the Operative to make it Irreducible. Next round, Deputy brings out a Crooked Cop, heroes with the AoE can still it Operative for full damage.

Marginal.  Fixer of course has significantly increased value in a fight with his nemesis, but Riveting Crane is still not especially strong there.  It only ever works if Fixer can get through, and the odds of other heroes not being able to get through if he can are fairly slim, considering most of them do more damage than him with anything less than a perfect setup.

Spite has his DR drug for the first hit every round, Fixer can Charge or Overdrive first, then the second hit will do damage and no one else has to worry about the DR.

A slight advantage, but noteworthy.  When I'm done being utterly sick of Spite, I'll try to remember Fixer against him.

Hitting Apostate or Dawn everyone round would mean a Fiendist Pugilst or Citizen Anvil won't apply their DR to them.

Handy, but again, only 1 DR, so not spectacular.

Kismet's Shaky Arm on anyone other than Fixer, Striking makes Shaky Arm not matter.

Again, good point, but Shaky Arm targets the hero with most cards in play.  Whether that's Fixer or not depends on a lot of factors; his "kit" is almost never more than four cards, but he absolutely must have at least two.  Except for Wraith and Adept, almost every hero can be effective with just one card in play, so the odds are fairly decent that Fixer with a Style, a Tool, and Harmony or Bloody Knuckles is going to be the one with the Shaky Arm.

Akash'Bhuta's advanced flip side, someone can reduce her End of Turn damage, while Fixer can make all limb damage is still doing it's full amount.

I'm not even sure what this is meant to be saying, you appear to have tripped over your own grammar here.  (Not judging, it happens to the best of us.)

Fighting in Pike Industrial, The Block, or Time Cataclysm, DR can come out, but Fixer having Striked, it won't matter to that target.

Good point there; I do tend to forget about Environment DR being as ir-reducible as any other kind (as I already mentioned before with Mega Computer).

Even funner in the Pike Industrial, if both Biometic and Irradiated Vats come out, canceling each other out, Fixer can Strike and then every other hero will get the +1 towards that target.

That is indeed funny.

As I pointed out in another thread, Wraith's Mega Computer and Fixer's Riveting Crane are a great combo together. So Riveting Crane is not a Blank Card, you just have to be clever in your uses for it.

I believe my original statement was that it was blank about half the time, and you didn't disprove that by mentioning about half of the villains, with many of the cases you brought up being fairly infrequent things.  Baron Blade, La Capitan, Matriarch, Gloomweaver, and Plague Rat have only tiny amounts of DR from one or two cards, hardly worth acknowledging (except on BB's flipside advanced, but with only 30 HP that's pretty irrelevant).  Miss Info has huge DR which Fixer will struggle to ever get through, though if he manages it, the team's chances improve drastically - assuming of course that Fixer survives her retaliation damage, or else Riveting Crane will go away when he incaps.  Iron Legacy might have DR, but it's ultimately his healing which is the bigger problem, and ditto with Spite.  The Ennead have one member with DR, though she will usually turn up eventually; usually it's simple enough to just kill her, but I can definitely see it being worth Fixer's time to punch through against someone else who's at lower HP and doesn't heal like Nuit does.  Still, this is a lot of marginal cases.

The point about Advanced games is a fair one, perhaps as I play those more often (and stop forgetting about the DR), I'll gain more appreciation for Fixer.  But I still think he has to work too damn hard to be halfway-competent, when other heroes can be amazing with that much effort, or equally competent with almost none.

Pretty much worthless? Did you not see my post where I stated I went an entire game with Driving Mantis in play and was still kicking ass? Heroes were bouncing their second target off Fixer, Environment and Villain were unable to touch him. He was getting insane with his redirection. Grease Monkey Fist would be fine as the only card in paly as well.

GMF gets him up to two damage; I wouldn't stop there, at least not without AZ or somone in play to care about the shifting damage types.  Mantis is a fun card, but the 2-damage cap keeps it from being amazing in my experience, as hits for 3 or 4 are usually what I'm worried about.

Bcause every hero needs a search card to find every card in the deck!

If they're not competent without that card, then yeah.  Chrono-Ranger is definitely one of the best decks in the game, because he has tons of situational singletons and two different search cards for finding them, which also do a damage on top of the searching.  Maybe I'm a little spoiled, but Fixer looks pretty gorram pathetic next to that.  Heroes like Tempest or Tachyon, of course, don't need a search card because every card in their deck is good, just about.  Again, Fixer wishes he could say the same.  The only hero I identify as being in about the same "league" as Fixer is Bunker (and poor Expat is in a league all by herself below that).  Both need immense setup for fairly mediocre results, and of the two, Bunker is marginally more to my taste, partly for flavor reasons (BUDDABUDDABUDDA) and partly because of my long history of atrocious luck with Fixer.

Ra is a hero that is solely about burning a target. There isn't much else for him to do.

And with the exception of a few matches like Miss Info or Wagner Mars, there isn't much need for him to do anything else.  Fixer might solve problems, but Ra ignores them entirely more often than not, by simply melting the main villain's face as quickly as metahumanly possible.

Fixer takes a different mind set than Ra to play.

I have only one mindset with which to play all heroes.  Perhaps Fixer is just less to my taste than most.  (Ra is not necessarily the most so, but at least he's at or above the median.  My ideal is probably Scholar or Nightmist, as both of them have won all but I think 3 games out of 16 or so.)

Because he is built to burn, burn, burn.

Yes, he does one thing and he does it well.  While Fixer does one thing (whack, whack, whack) and does it mediocre.

Sure, by your definition. My definition is he has cards that are ready to be used yet!

Good luck living that long.  28 HP isn't awful, but it isn't great either, and all villains will generally kill the entire party within an average of perhaps 8 turns, unless measures are taken to the contrary.

When you put the same 10 cards on top of your deck, it sure is going to be hard to draw anything else.

Well it's not like I've been doing it on purpose.  Like I said, equally bad shuffles for all other heroes have turned out consistently better, except for Expatriette, Fanatic and AZ (with, oddly, Tempest being probably the next-worst, but by a fairly substantial gulf).

But Fixer isn't solely about doing damage every round.

As opposed to what else?  Standing around sucking his thumb?  He can't destroy Ongoings, he can't help allies draw cards or stack their decks, he can't control the villain deck, he can only draw cards himself if he lucks into Tool Box.  If he gets Driving Mantis and/or Pipe Wrench he can tank a little, but is nowhere near as good at it as Scholar, Legacy, or even fanatic.  Otherwise, damage is pretty much all he's good for.

If you are trying to play Fixer as Ra, then yes you will be very dissapointed. That's equal to playing Tachyon as Visionary, wondering why you can't manipulate decks.

Visionary is nowhere near as exclusively about manipulating decks as I'd like (except for Dark visionary, where she's too much so).  Perhaps part of my problem with Fixer is just that I got into him later; my early games with Visionary might have convinced me she's about nothing but dealing pathetic amounts of psychic damage.  Still, the time difference involving them isn't that huge.  Anyway, Tachyon is very good at telling you what her deck should be about, AND, and this is the big "and", she gives you pretty much every tool you could possibly wish for to enable her to do what she does.  Fixer can't even come close to such a boast.

Doing high damage is not what Fixer is all about.

Well, there you go; that's exactly what my problem is with him.  He can't do much of anything other than do damage, and he can't even do that especially well, and has to work very hard to manage that much.  If his deck was about putting Car targets into play and then repairing them so that other heroes can drive them, he might well be able to contribute more effectively.  (On that subject, I'm not certain I've played him with Unity, and that's an obvious thing to try sometime.)

Things Mister Fixer can do other than specifically dealing damage:

  • Penetrating DR. 
  • Allowing others to penetrate DR.
  • Returning destroyed equipment to players' hands (while dealing extra instances of damage in the same play!)
  • Redirecting particularly common damage instances (2-3 damage).
  • Preventing all non-hero targets from dealing damage.
  • Changing damage type to preferred types.

Things Ra can do other than specifically dealing damage:

  • Putting cards from the Environment trash under the Environment deck.
  • Healing himself 3 hp.
  • Making the party immune to fire damage (at the expense of dealing significant damage).
  • Providing a flat +1 damage buff.

 

I've said it before and I'll say it again, Mister Fixer is not not not not not a "damage-oriented" hero.  Ra, Haka, Expatriette, and even Bunker will consistently out-damage Fixer.  That's fine, because it's not his primary role.  He's there to "fix" the situations that come up as they arise.  Need an "off-tank"?  He can do that.  Need some global damage?  Pull out the Crowbars or the Jack Handle.  Need to punch through DR?  He's got that handled.

Case in point:  this evening, my game group played a game with Legacy, Wraith, Expatriette, and Fixer against Apostate.  Fixer flopped Riveting Crane in Round 1 and attacked Condemnation.  Legacy's Galvanize got a single point of damage through, but that allowed the rest of the group to take out Apostate's sword that much faster, depriving the villain of significant damage.  This was exacerbated when Fixer threw down a Jack Handle, ripping through the Runes of Malediction/Orb of Delerium pair with ease.

Fixer's damage cannot be your only focus when playing him.  If you think that way, you'll be disappointed.  Fixer's damage is just the "delivery device" for the various benefits provided by his Styles, Tools, and One-Shots.  Fixer's power lies in what he offers the party:  he's a support hero, in disguise as a melee bruiser.

You guys are missing my point.  This is still a tiny percentage of all the cards in the game; damage type is still largely irrelevant in spite of all these effects.  In order for me to consider Haka's and Ra's powers different, there would have to be virtually zero occasions on which they affect the game in the same way.  You'd have to have either tons of extra rules text on cards, saying that the Stout Barrel takes extra damage from fire and that Old Lady in the Street reduces all melee damage by 1 because she's a half-solid ghost, or else have rules baked into the game that says all fire damage causes things to burn for an additional 1 damage each round until something extinguishes the flame, but that melee damage represents being physically close to the target and thus you're also affected by splash damage from any area effect which hits them.  The point being, the effects of damage type would have to be interlaced through the entire game in a completely inescapable fashion, resulting in an overwhelming increase of complexity, comparable to a miniatures wargame or an RPG.  I am not suggesting that anything like this should happen, of course - but because it has not, damage type is largely irrelevant in the game, and thus two powers having different damage types does not make them different powers.

(For that matter, two powers dealing different amounts of damage doesn't really make them different powers; Haka and Mr. Fixer both punch things, Parse and Chrono-Ranger both shoot things.  I would however say that dealing different numbers of damage instances is a unique power; Tempest is not like CR, because CR is shooting one thing while Tempest is making a mild storm which pelts everyone with debris.  Likewise, Fanatic's Exorcism feels different from Fixer's strike, even though a component of it is exactly the same, because it has another component - no other hero has a "deal 1 damage each of 2 different types to the same target" power, but if Captain Cosmic turns out to have "Captain Cosmic deals one target 1 projectile damage and 1 energy damage", I would consider that to be the same power as Fanatic, and if he could deal the damage to two different targets, I'd consider it the same as F6 Wraith.)

The point I'm trying to make is that If the company had ever personally promised me that no two powers would be duplicated, I'd consider Haka and Ra alone to be proof that they weren't honoring the spirit of that agreement, and I am very much not a "letter of the law" kind of guy.  As far as I'm concerned, if they aren't prepared to deliver on a common-sense interpretation of such a statement, they should never have made that statement.
